# Simplified Technical English

Write all documents in Simplified Technical English (STE). STE is a controlled language. It makes technical text clear for all readers, including readers who do not have English as a first language. It is based on [ASD-STE100](https://www.asd-ste100.org/). For an introduction, see [Simplified Technical English on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Technical_English).

These rules apply to prose. They do not apply to code, commands, file names, quotes or the names of standards and products.

## Words

1. Use one word for one meaning. Use the same term each time. Do not change it for variety.
1. Use the simple word. See the table below.
1. Use a word with only one meaning in each document. Example: "test" is a noun. To make a verb, write "do a test".
1. Do not make a noun phrase of more than three words. Change "patient appointment reminder message template" to "the template for appointment reminders to patients".
1. Write the full term for each acronym the first time you use it in a document. Example: "patient administration system (PAS)".
1. Do not use slang, idioms or marketing words.

## Sentences

1. Write short sentences. An instruction has a maximum of 20 words. A description has a maximum of 25 words.
1. Use the active voice. Use the passive voice only when you do not know who does the action.
1. Use simple verb tenses: present, simple past and simple future. Do not write "will have been done".
1. Write one instruction in each sentence.
1. Start an instruction with a verb. Example: "Record the decision in the decision log."
1. Do not remove words such as "the", "a" or "is" to make a sentence shorter.
1. Use "-ing" words only as names of things, such as "testing" in "the testing plan".

## Paragraphs and structure

1. Write one topic in each paragraph.
1. Do not write more than six sentences in a paragraph.
1. Use numbered lists for steps that you do in sequence.
1. Use bullet lists for items that have no sequence.
1. Use tables to compare options.
1. Put the most important information first.

## Use this, not that

| Use | Do not use |
|---|---|
| use | utilise, leverage |
| start | commence, initiate, kick off |
| end, stop | terminate, cease |
| help | facilitate, assist |
| get | obtain, acquire |
| show | demonstrate, illustrate |
| make sure | ensure, ascertain |
| about | approximately, circa |
| before | prior to |
| after | subsequent to, following |
| because | due to the fact that |
| if | in the event that |
| to | in order to |
| now | at this point in time |
| must | is required to, it is mandatory that |
| can | is able to |
| more | additional |
| send | transmit |
| decide | make a decision |
| quick | expeditious |

## Words to avoid

- Vague words: "robust", "seamless", "simply", "just", "easily", "best-in-class", "world-class", "synergy".
- Words with many meanings: "address" as a verb (use "fix" or "answer"), "handle" (use "process" or "manage"), "issue" except for a GitHub issue (use "problem").
- Words that hide the actor: "it was decided". Write who decided.

## Check before you finish

- Did you write each sentence in 25 words or fewer?
- Did you use the same term for the same thing each time?
- Did you write the full term for each acronym the first time?
- Did you remove the marketing words?
- Can a reader who does not know the project understand the text?
